checks.note: reconcileOneStripeSubscription returns early only on paymentCoachSubscriptionRepository.findByStripeSubscriptionId and never checks paymentPlayerSubscriptionRepository.findByStripeSubscriptionId (which exists — see handleSubscriptionUpdated), so live player subscriptions reach the coach-only resolveCoachAndAlertIfOrphaned chain. The caveat holds: StripeCustomer is keyed by user id and shared — subscribeCoach and subscribePlayer both load stripeCustomerRepository.findById(userId), with no guard against one user holding both roles.

matches.note: R7 identifies pending changes surviving cancellation/grace expiry and applyPendingChanges re-granting a paid tier without a status check — same defect and consequence.
R6 identifies the default allow_incomplete behaviour plus unconditional tier persistence granting paid entitlement on a declined/incomplete first payment.
R14 covers resolvePlayerTierKey ignoring status and R6 explicitly names both CoachProfileService.getCoachSubscriptionTier and the quota reader as status-blind; jointly they cover F3.
R1 states downgrades only insert a change row and applyPendingChanges never calls Stripe, so billing stays at the old higher price — identical defect.
R10 identifies changeCoachTier/changePlayerTier allowing tier changes on PAST_DUE/CANCELLED rows with a lingering stripeSubscriptionId, same place and consequence.
R2 covers both halves: grace expiry never cancels Stripe (continued billing) and re-subscribe on the CANCELLED row creates a second orphaned Stripe subscription.
R3 states pastDueSince is only set when null and never reset on recovery, so a later failure is cancelled with near-zero grace — identical.
R13 covers only the missing event-ordering guard fragment; the CHECK-constraint violation/webhook retry loop for unmapped statuses and the missing invoice.paid handler are not reported.
R11 identifies entities loaded before the Stripe call being merged by @Transactional persist with no @Version, silently reverting concurrent webhook updates — same defect.
R4 identifies the sub-create-{customer}-{price} key replaying stale responses within 24h (plus the sibling-sharing variant), same root cause and consequence.
No reported finding mentions CREATE_PRORATIONS deferring the upgrade charge to the next invoice or the upgrade-then-cancel escape.

No reported finding covers the subscription.updated event arriving before persistCoachSubscription being acknowledged via the race-grace suppression and permanently lost; R12/R13 describe different races.
R5 reproduces the unnormalised tier defect exactly: valueOf throws outside the PessimisticLockingFailureException catch, rollback after Stripe charge, and the player 'pro' fallback-quota case.

unmatched_reported.note: Concrete trigger: locks released when the batch load commits, user upgrades (voiding the change) before the per-item apply, which still writes the stale toTier and merges voided_at back to null — a genuine concurrency defect distinct from F1.
Concrete trigger: double-click creates two pending change rows, LIMIT 1 voids only one and SKIP LOCKED can void none, so a stale downgrade later applies — not in the key.

Concrete trigger: two concurrent subscribes with different tiers (different idempotency keys) both pass the unlocked alreadyActive check, leaving an orphaned billing Stripe subscription — distinct from the sequential re-subscribe in F6.

Concrete trigger: two concurrent first requests both miss the find-then-insert, and the unique coach_id/player_id constraint turns one into an unhandled DataIntegrityViolationException.
